source_caption:
Christopher Nolan brilliantly roots the staggering, cosmic scale of his deep-space epic entirely within the intimate heartbreak of a father’s ultimate choice. The profound emotional engine of the film isn’t just about surviving a dying planet or navigating terrifying wormholes—it’s the devastating, agonizing sacrifice of leaving your children behind in the desperate hope of saving them. By making relativity a literal, physical obstacle, the story masterfully weaponizes time itself, transforming a terrifying journey into the infinite unknown into a heartbreaking, ticking-clock race to return before a family’s entire lifetime simply slips away.
⠀
Interstellar (2014), directed by Christopher Nolan, starring Matthew McConaughey, Anne Hathaway, Jessica Chastain. A desperate team of pioneering astronauts embarks on a perilous, mind-bending voyage through a newly discovered wormhole, racing against time to find a habitable new home and save humanity from a dying, dust-ravaged Earth.

source_details.title: Interstellar
source_details.synopsis: Interstellar is a 2014 epic science fiction drama film directed by Christopher Nolan, who co-wrote the screenplay with his brother, Jonathan Nolan. It features an ensemble cast led by Matthew McConaughey, Anne Hathaway, Jessica Chastain, Bill Irwin, Ellen Burstyn, and Michael Caine. Set in a dystopian future where Earth is suffering from catastrophic blight and famine, the film follows a group of astronauts who travel through space in search of a new home for humanity. The film began development in 2006 from a treatment by producer Lynda Obst and theoretical physicist Kip Thorne, and was originally set to be directed by Steven Spielberg.
